prediction_registered_before_running: if #24's artifact is the same phenomenon as #5's, its magnitude and site set are also deterministic per image, and reflashing an old image reproduces that image's numbers exactly
falsifier_registered: an image reflashed, hours apart with other images in between, giving materially different #24 magnitudes - which would say #24 is a genuine per-run draw and is NOT the same thing as #5
design: A-B-B-A over two images that #5 separates cleanly; 9 runs an image
conclusion: #24 is not image-locked. On the same statistic, the same bench and the same two images, #5's peak phase takes ONE value per image across 34 runs and #24's takes a fresh value every run - 9 distinct in 9, on both images. The two issues do not behave alike.
caveat: the #24 statistic is an argmax over a profile, and an argmax over a shallow profile wanders whether or not the underlying thing is stable. So this refutes image-locking for the argmax; a whole-profile comparison would be the stronger test. The contrast still stands, because #5's argmax on these same images does NOT wander.
also: #5 is preset M - the device drives its own DAC with the host removed - and #24 is the host-fed path, so this compares two setups as well as two issues. That is the point: the prediction assumed one phenomenon and the data says otherwise.
